out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Shellstock Label Marked, Last Date Served/Sold Info
violations.observation: The date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served is not recorded on the tag or label. Observed no dates on shellstock tags retained for mussels.
violations.corrective_action: The identity of the source of shellstock (oysters, clams, mussels) that are sold or served shall be maintained by retaining shellstock tags or labels and marking the tag or label with the date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served. Person in charge trained all employees on proper labeling for mussels. HONOO RAMEN BAR (Inspection Date: 08/20/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw salmon stored above cut kale in walk in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. Person in charge placed all raw animal foods below all foods that are ready to eat.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Restriction & Storage; Medicines Location
violations.observation: Employees' medicines are not properly located to prevent contamination of food and food contact surfaces. Observed personal prescription bottle stored on sushi line with food contact surfaces and other equipment.
violations.corrective_action: Employees' medicines shall be properly stored to prevent contamination of food and food contact surfaces. Person in charge placed all personal medications in designated storage.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: rice scoop stored in ambient temperature water between use; in use knife stored between 2 door prep (right) and prep table on cook line.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. Person in charge removed, cleaned, and properly stored all in use utensils.

violations.observation: The date when the last mussel shellstock from the container is sold or served is not recorded on the tag or label.
violations.corrective_action: The identity of the source of shellstock (oysters, clams, mussels) that are sold or served shall be maintained by retaining shellstock tags or labels and marking the tag or label with the date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served. Person in charge trained all staff on the proper labeling of all mussel shellstock after the last shellstock is sold from the batch.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw beef stored above zucchini and mushrooms in 2 door prep unit (R) on cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. Person in charge placed all raw items below all items that are ready to eat.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw chicken stored above raw scallops in walk in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). Person in charge placed all raw animal foods according to cook temperature. HONOO RAMEN BAR (Inspection Date: 02/24/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cut kale (59F) in 2 door prep on cook line (right side); cut lettuce (54F) in walk in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. Person in charge placed items to be properly cooled.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: PIC Duties, Train Employees on Handwashing
violations.observation: Poor handwashing procedures observed. The PIC did not properly demonstrate how to wash hands. She used her clean hands to turn off the water.
violations.corrective_action: The Person in Charge or certified food manager is responsible for monitoring his/her employees for proper hand washing procedures to ensure effective hand washing. THE EHS TRAINED THE MANAGER ON HOW TO PROPERLY WASH HANDS AND THE MANAGER TRAINED THE OTHER FOOD EMPLOYEES.

violations.title: Permit to Operate Posted in Conspicuous Location
violations.observation: The establishment has not posted the 2025 Food Establishment Health Department permit to operate in a conspicuous location.
violations.corrective_action: A valid permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a conspicuous place in the public view. Food establishment permits are issued for a calendar year and expire on December 31 regardless of the month of issue. EHS WILL EMAIL THE ADMIN STAFF TO OBTAIN A DUPLICATE COPY OF THE 2025 PERMIT. ONCE RECEIVED VIA EMAIL, PLEASE POST IT BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The EHS explained the importance of a vomit and diarrhea clean up policy and provided the manager with a copy of the FCHD model policy. HONOO RAMEN BAR (Inspection Date: 08/28/2025) Page 3 of 5

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: A food employee was observed eating, smoking, or drinking in areas where they may contaminate food, clean equipment, utensils or other items needing protection. Food employees were observed drinking from water bottles and containers in the food prep area and storing the bottles in the food prep refrigerators.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may only eat, drink, or use tobacco in a designated area like a dining room or office area. Employees shall not eat or drink in the kitchen areas, warewashing areas, or storage areas where items may become contaminated. Food employees may drink in the but it must be form a covered container with a straw.

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Parasite Destruction
violations.observation: The following fish offered for service or sale in the ready-to-eat form was not frozen to ensure parasite destruction: fresh fluke is received fresh and used in sushi/sashimi.
violations.corrective_action: Before service or sale in ready-to-eat form, raw or partially cooked fish shall be: 1) frozen and stored at a temperature of -4F or below for a minimum of 7 days in a freezer, or 2) frozen at -31F or below until solid and stored at -31F or below for a minimum of 15 hours, or 3) frozen at -31F or below until solid and stored at -4F or below for a minimum of 24 hours. *The EHS informed the manager that since there is no freezing of the fluke, that it may not be served raw or undercooked, and that it must be fully cooked to serve be served. She said she understood and would not serve the fluke as sushi. Ensure continued correction before the follow up.

violations.title: Shellstock Record System, Label/Tags
violations.observation: Observed no tag for fresh oysters and mussels stored in the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Shellstock tags shall remain attached to the container in which the shellstock are received until the container is empty. EHS HAD MANAGEMENT DISCARD. EHS DISCUSSED THAT THE FRESH SHELL STOCK SHALL BE RECEIVED FROM AN APPROVED SOURCE OFF THE ICSSL LIST, HAVE A TAG ATTACHED, DATE THE TAG ONCE THE LAST PIECE OF FRESH SHELL STOCK IS SOLD, AND RETAIN THE TAGS FOR 90 DAYS. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw chicken, fish and meat were stored next to each other in the top of one of the prep units and in the walk-in.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment were not observed sanitized: 1) 5 gallon container washed at the 3-vat sink but not sanitized.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. EHS DISCUSSED WITH THE MANAGER AND STAFF MEMBER TO SET UP THE SANITIZER AT THE 3-VAT SINK FOR ITEMS THAT WILL NOT FIT INTO THE DISH MACHINE FOR CHEMICAL SANITIZING. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: soups and sauces in the walk-in are held more than 24 hours and were not date-marked.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. Correct before the follow-up inspection.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food, Disclosure
violations.observation: The following raw and/or undercooked foods are provided on the menu, menu board, table tent or brochure without proper disclosure: most of the raw or undercooked foods were not disclosed properly on the menu. The establishment is using a blue fish logo to denote raw or undercooked menu items. To meet the requirement, the blue fish must appear next to the food ingredient, not the menu item, that is undercooked or raw. For example, the blue fish is next to the word jalapeño for the Yellowtail Jalapeño appetizer, which is incorrect. The blue fish must be next to the words, “slice yellowtail” to indicate that the yellowtail is the undercooked food item.
violations.corrective_action: The Consumer Advisory shall include a disclosure statement that includes a description of the animal-derived foods as raw/undercooked or identification of the animal-derived foods by asterisking (*) them to a footnote that states that the items are served raw or undercooked, or contain raw or undercooked ingredients. *Please update the menus to reflect this change. It is recommended that you have the EHS review the menu changes before printing to ensure they are correct. In the meantime, you could add blue stickers to each food ingredient that is served undercooked or raw on each menu item, and on each menu. Also, ensure that all others foods offered raw or undercooked are properly marked on the menu.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Thermometers, Easily Readable
violations.observation: The temperature measuring device located in/on the following equipment is not designed to be easily readable: the thermometer in the sushi display refrigerator was not legible and needs to be replaced.
violations.corrective_action: Temperature measuring devices shall be designed to be easily readable. Replace the thermometer with one that is legible within 6 months.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: several bulk food containers, some squeeze bottles, some other working containers.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. *Ensure all food containers, squeeze bottles, and bins are labeled before the follow up.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Ice As Coolant Not Used as Food
violations.observation: Ice used as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of food is also for beverage ice or used as food. At the bar ice bin used for drinks, there was a container with bar utensils stored in it.
violations.corrective_action: After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of food, packaged foods, beverages, or cooling coils/tubes, the ice may not be used as food. Ice can be used for food or cooling items, but not both. The manager removed the container with utensils in it from the ice bin.

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor in the walk-in, the kitchen the sushi prep area, and the bar.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS DISCUSSED ENSURING ALL ITEMS ARE 6 INCHES OFF THE FLOOR BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP USING APPROVED NSF SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Jewelry
violations.observation: Employees observed wearing jewelry on their arms and hands while preparing food.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall limit their jewelry to a plain wedding ring while preparing food. Food employees may not wear bracelets, watches, etc. because they can inhibit proper hand washing. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter in the kitchen on the food prep line.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. The manager moved the wet wiping cloth to a sanitizing solution bucket. HONOO RAMEN BAR (Inspection Date: 08/28/2025) Page 4 of 5

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: 1) bowls were being used to dispense foods in several areas; 2) the ice cream scoop was stored in standing water, 3) knives were wedged between equipment at the cook line.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. *The manager removed the bowls used for dispensing, she also removed the knives, and washed and sanitized the ice cream scoop to correct this. Ensure continued correction before the follow up.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equipment/Utensils Air Drying
violations.observation: Several pieces of clean equipment were found stacked while wet after cleaning and chemical sanitization.
violations.corrective_action: After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining before contact with food. *The EHS discussed this with the manager. Correct before the follow up.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers (seaweed salad containers) were observed reused for the storage of different foods.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. *Discontinue reusing the seaweed salad containers. Instead use approved commercial food containers.

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items Storage and Handling
violations.observation: Forks, spoons and soup spoons (plastic and tableware) were found handled, displayed or dispensed with the food or lip-contact surface facing upward and without handles lined up.
violations.corrective_action: Single-service items and cleaned/sanitized utensils shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of food and lip contact surfaces are prevented. Line up handles so food contact surfaces don’t have to be touched. Ensure continued correction before the follow up.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Corrosion-Resistant/Nonabsorbent Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not durable: 1) Aluminum foil lining surfaces.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be durable, corrosion-resistant, and nonabsorbent. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO REMOVE THE FOIL AS IT IS NOT CLEANABLE. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Equip/Utensils, Durable under Normal Use
violations.observation: Observed a noodle machine not identified as NSF approved or equivalent.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment and utensils shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions. EHS ASKED THE MANAGER TO REMOVE THE NOODLE MAKER OR FIND SPECIFICATIONS SHOWING IT IS NSF APPROVED OR EQUIVALENT. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: the hood systems and filters, the inside of the microwave, shelving under the cook line, interiors of refrigeration units, etc.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. EHS discussed more frequent cleaning. Ensure correction before the follow up.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed an unapproved splitter on the mop sink faucet.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. EHS had the manager take a picture of the approved pressure bleed valve. Manager ordered the approved part. Ensure it is installed before the follow up.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Mops Allowed to Air Dry
violations.observation: Observed that mops are improperly stored between use.
violations.corrective_action: Store mops in a position that allows them to air dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. EHS DISCUSSED WITH MANAGEMENT THAT WET MOPS SHALL BE HUNG TO ALLOW AIR DRYING AFTER USE. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.
